source_claims.claim: Problem 14.1 continues the Polya urn model from Problem 13.11 with positive initial white and black parameters w and b and first-i draw white counts X_i.
For i >= 1 and k in the displayed finite range, P(X_i = k) is the beta-binomial mass: choose(i,k) times the white and black rising factorials divided by the total rising factorial.
The random variable X_i / i is represented by scaling the finite white-count law by x -> x / i.
Using the Stirling/asymptotic route, X_i / i converges in distribution to the Beta(w,b) law.
